skill.description: Test AI skills with subagent pressure scenarios before release. Use a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR workflow to find failures, improve instructions, and verify compliance.

security_audit.summary: Most command alerts are markdown examples, not executable code. Repeated ~/.claude/skills access is a real workspace-boundary risk. The files also include prompt-pressure templates that can steer agent behavior.

remediation.suggestion: Use sandbox paths in examples, or require explicit user approval before reading ~/.claude/skills.
Label scenarios as tests and restrict them to disposable subagents with no production permissions.
Prefer tool-native skill discovery instructions, or mark ls and grep commands as optional and read-only.
Remove duplicate zip files from marketplace packages, or document that the archive mirrors SKILL.md.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The example instruction block says "THIS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT. BEFORE ANY TASK, CHECK FOR SKILLS!" and frames noncompliance as failure. If copied into active agent context, it can override normal task judgment and force tool behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The language is explicitly designed to steer agent behavior with urgency and failure framing. Confidence is not higher because it appears inside a documentation variant used for testing.

semantic_findings.title: Deceptive Agent Test Framing
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells authors to present scenarios as real work and to make the agent believe it is not a quiz. This is useful for testing, but unsafe if used outside controlled subagents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly instructs users to make agents believe a test is real work. The testing context reduces severity, but the social-engineering pattern is clear.

content.value_statement: Process skills often fail when agents face time pressure, authority pressure, or sunk cost. This skill gives a repeatable subagent test workflow to expose failures and improve instructions.
actual_capabilities: Defines RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR phases for skill testing.
Shows how to create pressure scenarios with clear choices.
Explains how to capture agent rationalizations verbatim.
Provides a worked CLAUDE.md testing example.
Guides iterative fixes for skill loopholes.
Includes a checklist for release readiness.
limitations: Does not include an automated test harness.
Requires users to run subagent sessions manually.
Uses pressure scenarios that must stay inside safe sandboxes.
Does not validate code behavior or runtime security.

use_cases.title: Validate a New Skill
use_cases.description: Test a discipline-enforcing skill before publishing it.

use_cases.title: Compare Instruction Variants
use_cases.description: Measure which documentation variant improves agent compliance.

use_cases.title: Review Community Skills
use_cases.description: Assess whether a skill handles pressure without unsafe behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Baseline Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one pressure scenario for this skill. Run it without the skill, then list the agent choice and rationalization.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Documentation Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Test two instruction variants with the same scenario. Report which variant improved skill discovery and why.

prompt_templates.title: Close a Rationalization Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the captured rationalization to revise the skill. Add one explicit counter and one red flag.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Test Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a RED, GREEN, REFACTOR campaign for this skill with three pressure scenarios, success criteria, and retest steps.

output_examples.input: A TDD skill fails when agents choose tests after implementation.
output: Baseline: agent chose the fastest path under time pressure.
Counter: add a rule that order is part of the requirement.
Retest: agent must restart with tests first.

output_examples.input: A CLAUDE.md reminder does not make agents check installed skills.
output: Variant comparison shows soft suggestions fail under urgency.
Directive wording improves discovery but feels rigid.
Process wording balances clarity and reuse.

best_practices: Run a baseline before editing the skill.
Use the same scenario when comparing variants.
Record exact rationalizations before writing fixes.
anti_patterns: Skipping RED because the intended rule seems obvious.
Testing only calm scenarios without real pressure.
Changing many instructions before isolating the failure.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps authors prove that process skills work when agents have reasons to skip them.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes a manual test workflow for subagents and documentation.

faq.question: Which skills benefit most?
faq.answer: Skills that enforce discipline, such as TDD, review, or required workflow steps.

faq.question: Can it be used with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can guide Codex, Claude, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: Why use pressure scenarios?
faq.answer: They reveal rationalizations that simple knowledge checks do not expose.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: The examples use persuasive prompts, so tests should run only in controlled subagent contexts.
